newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Macraes says cash costs above forecast.
newsitem.headline: Macraes says cash costs above forecast.

text.p: Gold miner Macraes Mining Company said on Thursday its cash costs for the March quarter were a higher than expected NZ$498 per ounce, due to the lower grade ore processed in the quarter.
March quarter production of 26,858 ounces was supplemented by reserves for sales of 30,150 ounces.
Macraes said production during the quarter was affected by the deferment of mining in Round Hill pit, advancement of mining in Innes Mills pit and development of Southern pit.

"Mill throughput has also been affected during the quarter by planned and unplanned maintenance downtime. During the first half of 1997, activities are focusing on the development of infrastructure and overburden removal to expose ore in the Frasers and Southern pits," it said.
Macraes said exploration continued to show encouraging results at the Macraes Gold Project, with continuing exploration success at Golden Bar, Round Hill and Innes Mills.
Resource consent hearings had started over its plans for expanding the project, with a decision and subsequent appeal period expected to be completed by June.

"Assuming the issue of appropriate consents and permits, we expect to begin construction of the project in the second half of the year of 1997 with a commissioning of the new mill late in 1998," Macraes said.
"We have, however, provided an allowance of a further nine months in our project schedule to accommodate possible delays to the resource consent process."
